DECOMPOSES BUT IS THE WRONG MOLECULE, so it must not be used. This is the ChEBI:8337 default_structure SMILES string verbatim. RDKit parses it as C20H12N4 (InChIKey AJYZYPAMLMSWHG-UHFFFAOYSA-N), two hydrogens short of the GEM formula, because ChEBI writes the pyrrole nitrogens as lowercase n with no [nH]. The decomposer accepts it with 4 nonzero groups. Pricing the GEM species from this decomposition would price a different species; the composition check in thermo_structure_attempt.py rejects exactly this case.

notes:
DOCUMENTED NEGATIVE. No measured or tabulated aqueous standard transformed Gibbs formation energy exists for porphine (the unsubstituted free-base macrocycle, C20H14N4, charge 0), and eQuilibrator's group decomposer refuses every valid spelling of it, so s_4022 and s_4023 stay unpriced. Recorded for completeness of the metabolite table only.

WHAT THE DECOMPOSER ACTUALLY DOES. Measured, not inferred: equilibrator_assets.group_decompose.GroupDecomposer raises GroupDecompositionError at group_decompose.py line 607 for the kekulized PubChem structure, the RDKit aromatic canonicalization of it, the cache's own stored SMILES for compound 2399, and the 21H,23H tautomer round-tripped from the ChEBI standard InChI. Kekulized vs aromatic and 21H,22H vs 21H,23H both change nothing. With raise_exception=False the decomposition covers the molecule with 8 nonzero group types and leaves exactly 2 atoms unassigned; both are aromatic carbons carrying three heavy neighbors and no hydrogen. Hypothesis (untested): those are the meso or alpha ring-fusion carbons of the macrocycle, for which the component-contribution group table has no entry. I did not confirm which positions they occupy in the ring system.

THE CACHE ENTRY IS MISLEADING AND SHOULD BE READ CAREFULLY. thermo_accession_sweep.json records has_group_vector=true for compound 2399, which reads as a successful decomposition. It is not one: the vector is present but EMPTY (0 nonzero entries out of a 163-long group basis) and ComponentContribution.standard_dg_formation returns None. The exclusion reason group_decomposition_failed is therefore correct, and the fresh-creation route in thermo_structure_attempt.py cannot rescue it, since the decomposer refuses the same structure the cache already holds.

A TRAP TO AVOID. The ChEBI:8337 default_structure SMILES string, C1=Cc2cc3ccc(cc4nc(cc5ccc(cc1n2)n5)C=C4)n3, DOES decompose (4 nonzero groups). It must not be used: RDKit reads it as C20H12N4, two hydrogens short of the GEM formula, because ChEBI writes both pyrrole nitrogens as bare lowercase n. The ChEBI standard InChI for the same entry is correct at C20H14N4; only the SMILES serialization is short. Any future attempt that feeds ChEBI SMILES straight to the decomposer will appear to succeed and will silently price a different species. thermo_structure_attempt.py's heavy-atom composition check does not catch this one, because the difference is in hydrogens only, which that check deliberately drops.

WHAT THE LITERATURE DOES HOLD, AND WHY IT IS NOT ADMITTED. The prior pass concluded only substituted-porphyrin solid-phase thermochemistry existed. That was too pessimistic: the NIST WebBook carries an entry for the UNSUBSTITUTED compound, species C101600, 21H,23H-porphine, CAS 101-60-0, C20H14N4, the exact molecule. It lists dfH(solid) = -1106.9 +/- 3.6 kJ/mol and dcH(solid) = -8764.1 +/- 1.8 kJ/mol (Longo, Finarelli, Schmalzbach and Alder 1970, J. Phys. Chem. 74, 3296-3297) and dsubH = 87 +/- 3 kJ/mol over 424 to 507 K (Stefanov, Stibor, Dominguez-Clarimon and Arndt 2004, J. Chem. Phys. 121, 6935). None of that is admissible here, for three independent reasons: it is an enthalpy, not a Gibbs energy; the condensed-phase value is the crystalline solid, not an aqueous species; and no entropy and no aqueous solvation free energy is tabulated, so there is no route from these numbers to a dGf'(aq) without computation. The NIST species index page lists exactly three data classes for C101600 (condensed phase thermochemistry, phase change, gas phase ion energetics) and no solution-phase or Gibbs-energy class, which is the direct evidence for the negative. Consistency check I ran on the NIST pair: dfH(solid) = 20*dfH(CO2,g) + 7*dfH(H2O,l) - dcH = -9871.0 + 8764.1 = -1106.9 kJ/mol, so the two rows are internally consistent under combustion to CO2, liquid water and N2. I did not adjudicate whether the 1970 measurement itself is correct, and nothing here depends on it.

WHY THIS ROW DOES NOT BLOCK ANYTHING. r_4337 (yeast-GEM 9.0.2 name "Iron-sulfur clusters transporter ATM1, mitochondrial", 7 participants) carries s_4022 at coefficient -1 and s_4023 at coefficient +1, verified in the model YAML. The species is the same molecule on both sides, so its formation energy cancels in the reaction energy and r_4337 prices from ATP hydrolysis alone once the code agent's cancellation-of-same-species rule lands. Caveat for that rule, flagged rather than resolved: the pipeline applies per-compartment pH, ionic strength and pMg (thermo_pipeline.py CompartmentConditions.for_compartment), so the cancellation is exact only for the untransformed formation energy. Whatever residual Legendre-transform difference remains between m and c is a transport term, not a formation term, and I did not measure its size for this species.
